items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: Phil Woods told a great story about how he was complaining about his horn... And Charlie Parker came in to the club and played his horn and blew him away

ctx.x: I don’t know. I don’t agonize over — Phil Woods told a great story about how he was complaining about his horn and couldn’t get it man. And Charlie Parker came in to the club and played his horn and blew him away, and he says, “Well I’m not going to complain about my horn anymore.”

I used to go around with Oscar Pettiford, every place he went he would always — if he didn’t have a lady with him — he would always say, “Come on let’s go hang.” And we’d go in the after hour joints during the day and in the evening you know and play. And I’d sit and watch him play and all like that. And the worst basses in the world. You know you © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
